title: Pressure-induced superconductivity in a bilayer metal
authors: Tomoya Sano, Satoshi Ikegaya, Shingo Kobayashi, Yasuhiro Asano
abstract: We propose a model that explains the mechanism of pressure-induced superconductivity in a bilayer metal. Four types of pair potentials are assumed for a Cooper pair consisting of two electrons on different layers. Absence of local inversion symmetry gives rise to the spin-orbit coupling which is antisymmetric in the two layers. We assume that external pressure enhances the hybridization between the two layers. The stability of the superconducting states is well explained by the frequency symmetry of the induced pairing correlations by these potentials. Pressure-induced superconductivity emerges when the following two conditions are realized. (i) The spin-orbit coupling induces the odd-frequency pairing correlations and suppresses superconductivity at ambient pressure. (ii) The interplay between the spin-orbit coupling and the hybridization induces the additional pairing correlation that belongs to an even-frequency symmetry class. We briefly discuss the relevance of our model to real materials.
summary: This work develops a theoretical model for pressure-induced superconductivity in bilayer metals, attributing the mechanism to the interplay between spin-orbit coupling and interlayer hybridization. By analyzing the symmetry of induced Cooper pair potentials, the authors show that PIS emerges when a specific even-frequency pairing correlation compensates for the SOC-induced suppression of superconductivity.
main_problem: The paper proposes a theoretical model to explain the mechanism of pressure-induced superconductivity (PIS) in a bilayer metal without relying on BCS enhancements of coupling constants or density of states.
main_result: PIS is predicted to occur when the interplay between spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and interlayer hybridization induces an additional even-frequency pairing correlation, stabilizing the superconducting state.
method: The analysis involves solving the linearized Gor'kov equation for the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian and calculating the superfluid weight ($Q$) to determine superconducting state stability.
model_or_system: The system is a bilayer metal where the Hamiltonian includes terms for interlayer hybridization ($t_\perp$) and SOC ($ oldsymbol{\alpha}_{\mathbf{k}}$). Four types of interlayer pair potentials are analyzed based on their frequency and symmetry properties.
key_observables: Superfluid weight ($Q$ or $q_F$), Critical Temperature ($T_c$), and the presence/magnitude of different pairing correlations (even/odd frequency).
important_parameters: Interlayer hybridization ($t_\perp$), SOC strength ($\alpha_R$), and external pressure (which enhances $t_\perp$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that SOC induces odd-frequency pairing that suppresses superconductivity at ambient pressure, requiring a second, even-frequency correlation to stabilize the state.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the bilayer structure, the dependence of $T_c$ and $q_F$ on $t_\perp$ for different pairing states (ESEE, ETEO), and the general mechanism of PIS.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes different pair potentials (ESEE, ETOE, ETEO) by solving the gap equation and calculating the superfluid weight, demonstrating how the interplay between SOC and hybridization drives PIS.
why_interesting: The focus on symmetry-protected pairing mechanisms (even vs. odd frequency) and the role of structural parameters (pressure/hybridization) to induce superconductivity is highly relevant to understanding unconventional pairing in correlated materials.

They couple with each other by the interlayer hybridization t⊥. The SOCs have opposite signs: αk in Layer 1 and −αk in Layer 2. (b): Uniaxial pressure along the z-axis decreases the interlayer distance. Such eﬀects are taken into account through the enhancement of the interlayer hybridization t⊥. (c): The pair potentials in this paper describe Cooper pairings between two electrons staying at diﬀerent layers.
